title: Vision AI in 2025 — Peter Robicheaux, Roboflow
talk_summary: A Roboflow ML lead argues vision models lag language models because vision benchmarks (ImageNet/COCO) are saturated pattern-matching tasks and vision-language pretraining (CLIP) lacks discriminative visual features, while pure-vision self-supervised pretraining (DINOv2) transfers much better. He introduces RF-DETR (DINOv2 backbone) and RF100VL, a 100-dataset domain-diversity benchmark where pretrained backbones and small fine-tuned specialists beat giant VLMs.

takeaways.technique: Domain-diverse eval suite instead of one saturated benchmark
takeaways.what_they_do: They built RF100VL from 100 hand-curated datasets across unusual domains (aerial, microscope, X-ray) because COCO's common classes make it too easy and unrepresentative of real capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Coco is too easily solvable... it basically has common classes like humans and like coffee cups
takeaways.numbers: 100 datasets; ~750k datasets screened; 10-shot splits per class

takeaways.technique: Small fine-tuned specialist beats giant generalist on narrow domains
takeaways.what_they_do: A YOLOv8 trained on only 10 examples per class outperformed a 72B state-of-the-art vision-language model on their benchmark.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you take a Coco or you take a YOLO V8 model and you train it on like 10 examples per class. It does better than like Quen V272
takeaways.numbers: 10 examples/class beats Qwen2.5-VL-72B; YOLOv8-nano 10-shot ~25 mAP vs zero-shot Grounding DINO ~19 mAP

takeaways.technique: Match model class to task; don't assume the biggest generalist wins
takeaways.what_they_do: They show VLMs generalize well linguistically but are 'hopeless' visually out-of-distribution, so task-appropriate specialist models win on narrow domains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: vision language models are really good right now at generalizing out of distribution in the vis in the linguistic domain but absolutely hopeless when it comes to generalizing in the visual domain

takeaways.what_they_do: They test whether a model actually uses class name + annotator instructions + 10 examples by deleting one input and checking if performance drops; no model currently benefits from all three.
takeaways.evidence_quote: no model exists that can leverage those three things and get higher map than if you just deleted one of those

takeaways.technique: Stronger embeddings/backbone transfer beats bigger task-specific training
takeaways.what_they_do: Swapping a DINOv2 pretrained backbone into a detector gave large gains on domain-diverse data versus training from scratch on a narrow dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: massive yields from using the Dynino V2 pre-trained backbone
takeaways.numbers: ~5-7 mAP gains from pretraining on transformer detectors vs ~0.2 for conv nets; large RF100VL gains
